summary: Weekend-buildable at zero cost, but demand evidence is all vendor blogs with no first-person manager complaint, and PMS vendors can add AI statement explanations natively. Talk to a few managers first; the idea isn't strong enough to spend a demand-test slot.

demand.evidence: Only vendor/consultancy blogs (Rentvine, Enterprise DNA); unsourced churn and time claims; RESEARCH.md found no manager complaint and no payment signal.

statusQuo.evidence: Hand-written owner emails or ChatGPT pasting; but unproven that small managers write explanatory letters at all.

specificity.evidence: Clear role and moment (ops manager, 50-300 doors, monthly close) but no named person or first-hand consequence.

wedge.evidence: CSV in, computed facts, model only phrases, human approves; shippable in days. Free first batch risks one-time use.

futureFit.evidence: PMS vendors can ship native AI statement summaries; verified-numbers approach differentiates only against chatbots.

premises: Small managers write or want per-owner explanatory letters (unsupported)
Owner confusion drives churn enough to pay $39-49/mo (vendor claim only)
The PMS portal is not enough (plausible, untested)
Managers will upload owner financials to a third-party tool (open trust question)
Reachable without sales calls via NARPM/Facebook groups/SEO (unproven)
alternatives: Minimal: free paste-a-statement letter tool with email capture, no accounts or storage
Ideal: multi-PMS presets, saved history, PDF/email send, Stripe
Lateral: template/prompt pack, or share covercheck's small-property-manager audience with a second offer
Recommended: talk to 3-5 managers first, then the minimal tool
wedge: One generic CSV upload, one plain-English letter per owner from code-computed facts, copy button; no history, accounts or payments.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby, Papa Parse, TS fact functions, free-tier LLM. Proof test: 3-owner CSV where owner A (2,000.00 income, 450.00 expenses, 160.00 fee) yields a letter with exactly 1,390.00, and no letter contains a figure absent from computed facts. PDF parsing and per-PMS mapping are the hidden cost.

risks: Demand evidence is vendor-sourced; the portal may be enough
PMS vendors add native AI summaries
Owner financial data trust and privacy; a wrong figure harms trust
Statement formats vary and PDFs are brittle
Free first batch invites one-time use
killCriteria: Drop if 3 conversations with 50-300-door managers show none writes explanatory letters, if a 14-day page gets fewer than 50 relevant visitors or 5 signups, if no manager will run a redacted real export, or if a major PMS ships AI statement explanations.
